answer: Since the island hash is stored at intake, the ocean graph groups the endorsements and the sable audit exposes the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 2 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. An operator copying one text across 195 aliases as a result pays for 195 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
